name: Family Butler
status: Calendar & modules · Shared parenting in beta
headline: More clarity. More togetherness.
summary: Organise family life together with a core calendar, childcare and a shared parenting module currently in beta testing.
title: A clearer view of family life.
description: Family Butler combines core calendar functionality with a childcare module and a shared parenting module. The shared parenting module is currently in beta testing. Together, we are developing practical support for everyday family life.
notice: The shared parenting module is currently in beta testing. We are looking for beta testers, developers and Apple TV developers.
goals: Simplify the organisation of family life

features.title: Core calendar
features.text: Calendar functionality is at the heart of Family Butler, supporting shared schedule organisation.

features.title: Childcare module
features.text: A dedicated module supports the organisation of childcare.

features.title: Shared parenting module
features.text: Support for shared parenting. This module is currently in beta testing.

name: stammbeiz.li
headline: Experience your local bar, virtually.
summary: A digital meeting place recreated the feeling of visiting a bar or restaurant during the COVID-19 period.
title: Coming together when meeting in person was hardly possible.
description: During the COVID-19 period and restrictions on movement, we supported and developed stammbeiz.li. Using SpatialChat, we recreated the rooms of two bars and restaurants online. Unlike an ordinary chat or closed group, guests could move freely through the rooms, join a table and talk to one another.
notice: A historical look back at a project from the COVID-19 period. SpatialChat, the beer tasting and the burger offer are not currently available.
goals: Enable people to meet when in-person gatherings were not possible
Recreate the spontaneous experience of sitting together in a bar or restaurant
Make shared experiences possible from home

features.title: Virtual rooms to move around in
features.text: Two bars and restaurants were recreated in SpatialChat. Guests could move freely, join tables and talk to one another.

features.title: Appenzeller beer tasting
features.text: An Appenzeller beer tasting was offered in one bar. The tasting set was sent to participants at home.

features.title: Burgers to collect
features.text: Burgers could be pre-ordered at the restaurant and then collected for takeaway.

name: Meet for Real
headline: Less swiping. More meeting.
summary: An idea for friendships and relationships where meaningful encounters matter more than time spent in an app.
title: Real connection instead of endless searching.
description: We’re exploring a matching service that helps people find compatible friendships and relationships. A good encounter should count — not the number of messages or the time spent in an app.
notice: Meet for Real is a working title and not yet an available service. Success criteria, consent, privacy and a fair pricing model still need to be clarified.
goals: Meaningful encounters instead of prolonged use
Transparency about real people and AI-based contacts
research: Preparation includes a fair comparison of existing apps: strengths and limitations, funding, actual costs, cancellation and transparency about AI contacts. Provider claims, verified facts and unconfirmed reports should be clearly separated. The app list and assessment are still pending.

name: Safe Steps
headline: Recognise fraud. Prevent it. Find guidance.
summary: A project idea for prevention and guidance: recognise fraud risks, understand ways to reduce them and find support after an incident.
title: Recognise fraud and be better prepared.
description: Safe Steps is an idea for clear information about how digital technologies are used for fraud and how people can recognise fraudulent tactics. It aims to support prevention and also help people who have experienced fraud make sense of the situation, understand possible next steps and find suitable support.
notice: Safe Steps is a working title and not yet an available advice service. Scope, specialist partnerships and possible fees still need to be clarified. Repayment cannot be guaranteed.
goals: Explain the risks of digital technologies and fraud schemes
Help people recognise warning signs of fraudulent tactics
Help people find guidance and suitable specialists after an incident
research: It remains to be explored what prevention information could help people recognise fraud attempts and reduce risks in everyday life. Information about digital technologies and current fraud schemes would need clear sources and expert review. Guidance, advice, referrals and post-fraud support would need to be clearly distinguished; protection from fraud or repayment could not be guaranteed.

name: Digital Media & Parenting
headline: Clear guidance. Confident parenting.
summary: Practical guidelines and recommendations for parents supporting their children’s use of digital media.
title: Helping parents navigate children’s digital lives.
description: We want to develop understandable, practical guidelines and recommendations for parents of children using digital media. The aim is to help families make informed decisions, discuss media use together and find an approach that fits their everyday lives.
notice: This is a project idea. The guidelines and recommendations have not yet been published; their scope and editorial review still need to be developed.
goals: Give parents clear, practical guidance on children’s use of digital media
Help families discuss media use and agree on everyday routines
Make topics such as age-appropriate content, privacy and online safety understandable
Bring parents’ experience and media education expertise together
research: We plan to bring together parents, educators and people with expertise in media education. Recommendations should be based on clearly identified sources, reviewed by suitable specialists and updated as digital media changes. The format and age groups are still to be defined.
